subject: OptiScale private offer — payment structure and rev-share request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@optiscale.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@optiscale.io
Date: 2028-07-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer request — payment terms + rev-share

Hi Rachel / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood’s latency profile. Our procurement/legal team flagged two items that are blocking final approval on our side and asked me to come back with a single ask to simplify internal sign-off: 

1) Payment timing: OptiScale requests Net90 for the first 12 months (we operate on a long billing cadence with legacy contracts).
2) Rev-share: because this will be a marketplace-driven integration, we are asking for a 35% rev-share for Marketplace-sourced usage for the first 12 months plus a $120k upfront credit to support onboarding.

We recognize these are outside typical Marketplace defaults. We want to confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a one-off structure — if needed, we can accept a phased rev-share (e.g., 40% first 3 months ramp to 35%) or provide a purchase commitment to offset the credit.

Attached is a short term-sheet with our ask (optiscale_revshare_proposal.pdf). Please advise the fastest path to get this exception approved. We are targeting a go-live on Aug 15 and have legal scheduled the end of next week for signatures.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Strategic Partnerships | OptiScale
+1 415-555-0192

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding OptiScale's request. TL;DR: Net90 for 12 months + 35% marketplace rev-share and $120k upfront credit. They offered a phased rev-share if that helps. Target go-live Aug 15, legal wants final terms next week.

Key facts: OptiScale is a mid-market analytics SaaS; projected first-year marketplace-attributed revenue ~ $1.2M based on their estimate. The $120k credit is to offset onboarding/marketing on AWS marketplace.

Can you evaluate options (payment terms, commission floor, impact to partner ops) and advise whether this is approvable under existing delegated thresholds or needs exec approval? I attached the proposal they sent.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim

Thanks for the heads up, Rachel — reviewed the attached proposal (optiscale_revshare_proposal.pdf). A few notes and an operational proposal to make this palatable: 

- Net90: this is outside standard Marketplace billing cycles. We can accept Net90 if OptiScale pre-funds a portion of the onboarding credit or provides a minimum committed spend (we typically use a deferred credit schedule). Proposed compromise: Net60 with a $60k holdback until the 90-day invoice clears, or Net90 if they increase upfront commitment by $60k.

- Rev-share: 35% is above our usual marketplace split for this tier. Suggest a stepped rev-share: 45% for months 1–2 (to compensate for the $120k), 35% months 3–12, and then re-evaluate at month 12 against realized ARR and quality metrics. Alternatively, we can do 40% first 3 months then 33% thereafter. 

- Upfront credit: $120k is large relative to expected contribution. We can structure as a marketing/onboarding credit tied to measurable milestones (listing, co-marketing asset, minimum monthly MAUs). If OptiScale commits to a 12-month minimum consumption (e.g., $800k TCV), we can amortize the credit.

I've attached a spreadsheet estimate of P&L sensitivity (optiscale_payment_schedule.xlsx). Please confirm whether this approach would be acceptable commercially, and if so I will prepare a short exception memo for exec review. If not, flag what flexibility we have on the numbers (they need an answer this week).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

Attachments: optiscale_payment_schedule.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: OptiScale private-offer exception ask (revenue & payment flow)

Lauren — escalating for exec consideration. Summary below and requested approval path.

Summary: OptiScale requests Net90 x12 + 35% rev-share + $120k onboarding credit. Our recommended one-off structure to protect Redwood economics: 
- Payment: Net60 with $60k holdback to be released after their first two invoices clear (or Net90 with $60k additional prepayment).
- Rev-share: 45% months 1–2, 35% months 3–12, with a 12-month review tied to disclosed Marketplace-sourced usage.
- Credit: $120k marketing/onboarding credit paid as reimbursements on milestone delivery (listing live, co-branded campaign, joint webinar).

Rationale: OptiScale's projected marketplace-attributed spend (~$1.2M) is material but concentrated; without milestones the credit and Net90 expose Redwood to cash flow risk. The stepped rev-share recovers cost while signaling partnership.

Requested ask: Executive sign-off needed for the stepped rev-share and Net90 concession (or confirm Net60 + holdback as an alternative). If approved, Deal Desk will issue a private offer and scoped DocuSign with those conditions.

Supporting links: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/OD-48291 (financial model + risk memo). Attached: optiscale_revshare_proposal.pdf, optiscale_payment_schedule.xlsx

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: optiscale_revshare_proposal.pdf, optiscale_payment_schedule.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: OptiScale private-offer exception ask (revenue & payment flow)

Thanks team — I reviewed the deal summary and the upside. Approve the compromise described by Deal Desk with one modification: we will accept Net90 conditional on OptiScale providing the additional $60k prepayment (total credited amount remains $120k) OR signing a $900k 12-month minimum commitment. The stepped rev-share is approved as: 45% months 1–2, 35% months 3–12, followed by a 12-month performance review.

Conditions: 
- All credits must be milestone-tied and reimbursed only upon evidence of delivery (marketing creatives live, AWS listing published, joint webinar executed).
- Legal to include a clawback clause if Marketplace-sourced usage is materially different from the forecast (>=30% variance) in first 6 months.
- Finance to confirm that Net90 with $60k prepayment does not breach cashflow covenants; if it does, default to Net60 + $60k holdback.

Marissa/Karthik: please prepare the exception memo and updated private-offer doc with these conditions and route to Legal & Finance. Rachel: share this decision with OptiScale and ask them to confirm which option they select (prepayment vs minimum commitment). Goal: get signatures by 7/26.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference
